vector-valued-functions-s1.title: The path of $\mathbf{p}(t) = \left\langle 2t, 6t - t^2 \right\rangle$
vector-valued-functions-s1.text: The tip of $\mathbf{p}(t) = \left\langle 2t, 6t - t^2 \right\rangle$ for $0 \le t \le 6$. The position vectors $\mathbf{p}(1)$ and $\mathbf{p}(4)$ are drawn from the origin.

table.caption: Position of a drone, in meters east (x) and north (y) of its depot, t seconds after takeoff

items.q: What is $\mathbf{p}(4)$, and what is its magnitude?

options: Magnitudes do not add component by component: $\sqrt{64 + 64}$, not $8 + 8$.

items.q: What is the displacement from $t = 1$ to $t = 4$?

options: This adds the positions; subtract them.

items.q: How far apart are the object's positions at $t = 1$ and $t = 4$?

mistakes.why: Use the length of the displacement, $\sqrt{6^2 + 3^2}$, not $6 + 3$.
$45$ is the length squared; take the square root.

items.q: What is the average rate of change of $\mathbf{p}$ on $[1, 4]$?

options: This is the displacement; divide by the $3$ units of time.
This divides $3$ by $6$; divide each component by the time.

items.q: The average rate of change of $\mathbf{p}$ on $[2, 4]$ is $\left\langle 2, 0 \right\rangle$. What does that mean?
options: The two positions have the same height, though it rose in between
The object moved straight right the whole time from $t = 2$ to $t = 4$
The object stopped moving up at $t = 2$
The object did not move between $t = 2$ and $t = 4$

why.correct: $\mathbf{p}(2) = \left\langle 4, 8 \right\rangle$ and $\mathbf{p}(4) = \left\langle 8, 8 \right\rangle$: same $y$, so the displacement is horizontal. In between, $\mathbf{p}(3) = \left\langle 6, 9 \right\rangle$ is higher.
options: Zero net change in $y$; the path still arches up to $y = 9$.
An average says nothing about the path in between; here it rose to $9$.
$x$ grew from $4$ to $8$, so it moved.

items.q: What is the drone's displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$?

options: Read both rows at $t = 10$ and subtract the start.
The components are swapped; east comes first.
This divides by $10$: that is a rate, not a displacement.

items.q: What is the average rate of change of the drone's position vector on $[5, 15]$, in meters per second?

options: This is the displacement; divide by the $10$ seconds.

items.q: How far is the drone from the depot at $t = 5$?

mistakes.why: Distance is the length of $\left\langle 40, 30 \right\rangle$: $\sqrt{40^2 + 30^2}$, not $40 + 30$.
$2500$ is the distance squared; take the square root.

items.q: On $[10, 15]$ the average rate of change of the position vector is $\left\langle 0, 10 \right\rangle$. Which statement does the table support?
options: At $t = 15$ the drone is due north of where it was at $t = 10$
The drone hovered in place from $t = 10$ to $t = 15$
The drone moved east and not north from $t = 10$ to $t = 15$
The drone flew a straight line due north the whole time

why.correct: $x$ is $60$ at both times and $y$ rose from $70$ to $120$, so the net move is due north. The table cannot show the path between readings.
options: $y$ rose by $50$ meters, so it did not stay put.
The east component of the rate is $0$.
Two readings give the net move, not the route in between.

items.q: For a vector-valued function $\mathbf{p}(t)$ drawn from the origin, what does the tip of $\mathbf{p}(t)$ trace as $t$ increases?
options: A circle centered at the origin
A straight line from the origin

why.correct: The tip is at $(x(t), y(t))$, so it traces the same curve in the same direction.
options: The tip is a point in the $xy$-plane, not on a $t$-axis.
Only for special functions, such as $\left\langle t, 2t \right\rangle$.

items.q: For $\mathbf{p}(t) = \left\langle 3 - t, 2t \right\rangle$, write $y$ as a function of $x$ for the path of its tip.

mistakes.why: Multiply all of $3 - x$ by $2$: $2(3 - x) = 6 - 2x$.

items.q: Which parametric equations describe $\mathbf{p}(t) = t^2\mathbf{i} + (1 - t)\mathbf{j}$?

why.correct: The $\mathbf{i}$ part is $x(t)$ and the $\mathbf{j}$ part is $y(t)$.
options: The square is on $t$ in the $\mathbf{i}$ part.

mistakes.why: Square the components, add, then take the root: $\sqrt{\frac{3}{4} + 1}$.
$\frac{7}{4}$ is the magnitude squared; take the square root.

items.q: What does $\left\| \mathbf{p}(t) \right\| = 4$ for every $t$ tell you about $\mathbf{p}(t) = \left\langle 4\cos t, 4\sin t \right\rangle$?
options: Its tip stays $4$ units from the origin: a circle of radius $4$
Its tip moves $4$ units for each unit of time, along a straight line
Its tip stays at one point, $4$ units from the origin
Its tip traces a circle of radius $16$

why.correct: $\sqrt{16\cos^2 t + 16\sin^2 t} = 4$: every position is $4$ units from the origin, and the direction changes with $t$, so the tip goes around a circle.
options: Constant distance from the origin, changing direction.
The length of $\mathbf{p}(t)$ is a distance from the origin, not a step size.
The direction changes with $t$, so the tip moves.

items.q: A new function is $\mathbf{q}(t) = \mathbf{p}(t) + \left\langle 2, 0 \right\rangle$. Compared with $\mathbf{p}$, predict each change.

variables.name: The $x$-coordinate of the position at each $t$
variables.why: Each position moves $2$ units right, so every $x$-coordinate grows by $2$.

variables.name: The displacement on any interval $[t_1, t_2]$
variables.why: The added $\left\langle 2, 0 \right\rangle$ appears in both positions and cancels when you subtract.

variables.name: The average rate of change vector on any interval
variables.why: It is the displacement divided by the time, and neither changes.

why.correct: A constant shift moves the whole path but leaves every difference of positions alone.

items.q: Put the steps for finding the average rate of change of $\mathbf{p}$ on $[t_1, t_2]$ in order.
options: Divide each component of the displacement by the elapsed time

why.correct: Positions, then their difference, then the time, then divide component by component.
